**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stalk (two stalks shown side by side, cut to expose the section)
- **Key features**:
  - Distinct **shiny black discoloration of the stalk rind** forming large blotches/streaks
  - Surrounding tissue is tan to orange-yellow
  - The dark lesions have merged into broad dark patches along the stalk
  - Some whitish areas visible (possible mycelium or degraded pith)
  - No tiny pinhead pycnidia (rules out Diplodia), no gray charcoal-like granular tissue (rules out Charcoal rot), no soft slimy rot (rules out Bacterial stalk rot), no black nodes snapping cleanly (rules out Physoderma stalk rot)

**Top candidate: Anthracnose_stalk_rot**

The hallmark feature of Anthracnose stalk rot is the **distinctive shiny black discoloration of the stalk rind**, with dark water-soaked lesions that coalesce into large black blotches or streaks. Both stalks in the image show exactly this pattern — large, glossy black areas on the rind with tan/yellow surrounding tissue. This is highly characteristic and distinguishes it from all other stalk rots in the class list.
